concept.name: Rally
concept.definition: A period of sustained price increases over days to months. Rallies occur within both bull and bear markets; a rise within a dominant downtrend is a bear market rally — a counter-trend advance, not necessarily the start of a recovery.
concept.intuition: A stretch where buyers dominate and prices climb, whether as the main trend or as a pause inside a larger decline.
concept.mechanics: Identified simply as a sustained sequence of rising prices; context is what classifies it — a rally that keeps printing higher highs and higher lows within an uptrend is trend continuation, while a sharp multi-week rise under a falling primary trend is read as a potential bear market rally driven by short covering and oversold conditions.
concept.failure_modes: Bear market rallies routinely suck in buyers and then fail at resistance, resuming the decline; only hindsight distinguishes them from new bull legs.
concept.misconceptions: That a strong multi-week rally proves the bottom is in; 2022 produced several large bear market rallies that each resolved to new lows.
concept.example: During the 2022 bear market, the S&P 500 staged several multi-week rallies amid Fed rate hikes; each faded and the downtrend resumed.

citations.source: Real Investment Advice — A Bear Market Rally? Or, Just A Correction?
